name: IN-07
label: Safe D

key_factors: District's strong Democratic lean of about 21 points
Incumbent André Carson running with over $1 million raised and $621,000 on hand
Republican challenger Patrick McAuley shows no reported fundraising
Prediction markets price Carson at roughly 97% to win
model.rationale: This Indianapolis-based seat leans heavily Democratic, and Carson is a well-funded long-time incumbent facing a challenger with no visible fundraising or outside support. Markets and fundamentals both point to an easy Democratic hold, so the forecast stays near the fundamentals-based expectation of a mid-twenties margin.
model.watch: A surprise would require a major late shift in the national environment or unexpected opposition spending, neither of which is currently in evidence.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
André Carson, a Democrat who has held this Indianapolis-area seat since 2008, is running for reelection against Republican Patrick McAuley and Libertarian James Sceniak. The district's partisan lean favors Democrats by roughly 21 points, giving Carson a substantial structural advantage.

Carson has raised about $1 million and holds $621,000 in cash, while no fundraising figures are reported for his challengers. Prediction markets on Kalshi and Polymarket both price Carson's chances at about 97 percent. No public general-election polls are available, but the combination of the district's lean, Carson's incumbency, and his financial edge points to a comfortable Democratic win.
